exact_results: For actual alpha : iota -> Nat on a finite coordinate type, multiindexCoordinateWord alpha is a fixed word indexed by Fin(sum_i alpha_i).
For every real weight, product_j weight(word_j) equals product_i weight_i^(alpha_i).
With DecidableEq iota for the literal finite filter, the number of j with word_j=i equals alpha_i for every coordinate i.
proof: The existence theorem converts the actual exponent function through Finsupp.equivFunOnFinite.symm and invokes the proved monomial_exponent_word_exists at M=Real. Finsupp full sum/product identities restore zero entries. Classical.choose fixes a representative. The occurrence-count theorem applies the exact product identity to weight two at one coordinate and one elsewhere; equality of the resulting powers of two implies equality of the actual filter cardinality and exponent.
semantic_checks: The length is the literal sum of the actual finite multiindex; no arbitrary length or assumed count enters the result.
The count of each coordinate is proved, so the chosen word has the advertised multiplicities, beyond merely satisfying a norm bound.
Empty coordinates and the zero multiindex produce zero length; the product identity uses empty products equal to one. Zero weights and zero exponents are included.
The count theorem explicitly carries DecidableEq iota to form the finite equality filter; in the intended Fin 3 + Fin d instance this is the ordinary available equality instance.
choice_disclosure: The fixed word uses Classical.choose, has no advertised intrinsic ordering, and is not an executable word-generation algorithm. No bit complexity is claimed.
